authorization: Owner requested source-checked research summaries and corrections on 2026-11-11.
review_method: Compared the full ScholarCatalyst and EM-DETR papers on arXiv with the generated Brief fields, including methods, results and limitations.

research.reason: The generated summary says researchers labeled queries and that the evaluation corpus was changing. The authors verified 894 questions and judged papers; the measured retrieval used a fixed local corpus. Replace implications about operational research outcomes with the study's measured retrieval result.

after.what_happened: In a test built from 184 lead authors’ judgments about 207 computer science projects, search systems tried to find earlier papers that could inspire work on 894 early-stage questions. A similarity-based search system found 48% of credited papers among its top 20 results.
after.why_it_matters: The test shows that search methods can miss papers researchers credit as useful for forming a new idea, even when search agents make repeated queries.
body_paragraphs: Lead authors of 207 recent computer science projects reviewed 894 questions about their projects before the key findings. They judged which earlier papers did or could have helped, including papers they had not encountered.

Search agents recovered 42% of credited papers in their top 20, compared with 48% for a similarity-based search system. Each question searched a fixed corpus limited to papers available before the project.
after.limitation: The labels depend on authors looking back at completed projects. The test used a fixed local paper corpus and no live web access, so its results do not measure research outcomes in practice.
after.headline: Search tools miss papers researchers say could inspire new work

research.reason: The generated EM-DETR summary described an unclear 'large open system' and claimed difficult findings can slow learning. The paper reports a student-teacher labeling method and limited gains for atelectasis; it does not establish a slowdown or clinical performance.

after.headline: Combining medical image datasets improves some lesion detection tests
after.deck: Researchers combined datasets with different labels; detection gains varied by finding in the reported tests.
after.what_happened: Researchers trained separate models on four medical image datasets, used them to fill missing labels, and trained a combined detector. Compared with a single-dataset detector, the new model improved detection on several chest X-ray and mammography findings. Gains were limited for atelectasis.
after.why_it_matters: The tests show a way to combine datasets with different labels, but they do not establish how the model would perform in clinical use.
body_paragraphs: Separate models predicted missing findings in the other datasets. The final model learned from both expert annotations and these generated labels, aiming to retain what each dataset contributed.
The combined model improved detection for several findings in the reported tests. Atelectasis showed smaller gains because its labels can overlap with other conditions and vary across datasets.
after.limitation: The study tested selected chest X-ray and mammography datasets. Improvements varied by finding, and the paper does not report a clinical deployment.
